arxiv-1703-03831.title: User Longevity and Engagement in Mobile Multiplayer Sports Management Games
arxiv-1703-03831.creator: Daniele Grassi, Giacomo Barigazzi, Giacomo Cabri
arxiv-1703-03831.description: Abstract Mobile games are extremely popular and engage millions of people every day. Even if they are often quite simple, their development features a high degree of difficulty and requires close attention to both achieve a high satisfaction from users and grant a return to the developers.

arxiv-2010-00735.title: Cycle-Consistent Adversarial Autoencoders for Unsupervised Text Style Transfer
arxiv-2010-00735.creator: Yufang Huang Wentao Zhu Deyi Xiong Yiye Zhang Changjian Hu Feiyu Xu
arxiv-2010-00735.description: Abstract Unsupervised text style transfer is full of challenges due to the lack of parallel data and difficulties in content preservation. In this paper, we propose a novel neural approach to unsupervised text style transfer which we refer to as Cycle-consistent Adversarial autoEncoders (CAE) trained from non-parallel data.

arxiv-2103-16294.title: On the relative power of linear algebraic approximations of graph isomorphism
arxiv-2103-16294.creator: Anuj Dawar, Danny Vagnozzi
arxiv-2103-16294.description: Abstract We compare the capabilities of two approaches to approximating graph isomorphism using linear algebraic methods: the invertible map tests (introduced by Dawar and Holm in [ DH12 ] ) and proof systems with algebraic rules, namely polynomial calculus , monomial calculus and Nullstellensatz calculus .

arxiv-2205-00069.title: Birds’ Eye View: Measuring Behavior and Posture of Chickens as a Metric for Their Well-Being.
arxiv-2205-00069.creator: Kevin Hyekang Joo, Shiyuan Duan, Shawna L. Weimer, Mohammad Nayeem Teli
arxiv-2205-00069.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Kevin Hyekang Joo, Shiyuan Duan, Shawna L. Weimer, Mohammad Nayeem Teli. Chicken well-being is important for ensuring food security and better nutrition for a growing global human population. In this research, we represent behavior and posture as a metric to measure chicken well-being. With the objective of detecting chicken posture and behavior in a pen, we employ two algorithms: Mask R-CNN for instance segmentation and YOLOv4 in combination with ResNet50 for classification.

arxiv-2405-03776.title: Near-optimal decoding algorithm for color codes using Population Annealing
arxiv-2405-03776.creator: Fernando Martínez-García, Francisco Revson F. Pereira, Pedro Parrado-Rodríguez
arxiv-2405-03776.description: Abstract The development and use of large-scale quantum computers relies on integrating quantum error-correcting (QEC) schemes into the quantum computing pipeline. A fundamental part of the QEC protocol is the decoding of the syndrome to identify a recovery operation with a high success rate.

arxiv-2410-02654.title: Deconstructing Recurrence, Attention, and Gating: Investigating the transferability of Transformers and Gated Recurrent Neural Networks in forecasting of dynamical systems
arxiv-2410-02654.creator: Hunter Heidenreich, Pantelis R. Vlachas, Petros Koumoutsakos
arxiv-2410-02654.description: Abstract Machine learning architectures, including transformers and recurrent neural networks (RNNs) have revolutionized forecasting in applications ranging from text processing to extreme weather. Notably, advanced network architectures, tuned for applications such as natural language processing, are transferable to other tasks such as spatiotemporal forecasting tasks.

arxiv-2502-15218.title: ESPnet-SpeechLM: An Open Speech Language Model Toolkit
arxiv-2502-15218.creator: Jinchuan Tian, Jiatong Shi, William Chen, Siddhant Arora, Yoshiki Masuyama, Takashi Maekaku, Yihan Wu, Junyi Peng, Shikhar Bharadwaj, Yiwen Zhao, Samuele Cornell, Yifan Peng, Xiang Yue, Chao-Han Huck Yang, Graham Neubig, Shinji Watanabe
arxiv-2502-15218.description: Abstract We present ESPnet-SpeechLM, an open toolkit designed to democratize the development of speech language models (SpeechLMs) and voice-driven agentic applications. The toolkit standardizes speech processing tasks by framing them as universal sequential modeling problems, encompassing a cohesive workflow of data preprocessing, pre-training, inference, and task evaluation.

arxiv-2510-07340.title: SpotDiff: Spotting and Disentangling Interference in Feature Space for Subject-Preserving Image Generation
arxiv-2510-07340.creator: Yongzhi Li, Saining Zhang, Yibing Chen, Boying Li, Yanxin Zhang, Xiaoyu Du
arxiv-2510-07340.description: Abstract Personalized image generation aims to faithfully preserve a reference subject’s identity while adapting to diverse text prompts. Existing optimization-based methods ensure high fidelity but are computationally expensive, while learning-based approaches offer efficiency at the cost of entangled representations influenced by nuisance factors. We introduce SpotDiff, a novel learning-based method that extracts subject-specific features by spotting and disentangling interference.

arxiv-2512-02914.title: Martingale Score: An Unsupervised Metric for Bayesian Rationality in LLM Reasoning
arxiv-2512-02914.creator: Zhonghao HeUniversity of Cambridge zh378@cam.ac.uk, Tianyi QiuPeking University qiutianyi.qty@gmail.com, Hirokazu ShiradoCarnegie Mellon University shirado@cmu.edu, Maarten SapCarnegie Mellon University maartensap@cmu.edu
arxiv-2512-02914.description: Abstract Recent advances in reasoning techniques have substantially improved the performance of large language models (LLMs), raising expectations for their ability to provide accurate, truthful, and reliable information. However, emerging evidence suggests that iterative reasoning may foster belief entrenchment, rather than enhancing truth-seeking behavior.

arxiv-2601-07309.title: ARM: Role-Conditioned Neuron Transplantation for Training-Free Generalist LLM Agent Merging
arxiv-2601-07309.creator: Zhuoka Feng 1*, Kang Chen 1*, Sihan Zhao 1**, Kai Xiong **, Yaoning Wang 1** Minshen Yu 1, Junjie Nian 1, Changyi Xiao 1, Yixin Cao 1,2 † \dagger, Yugang Jiang 1
arxiv-2601-07309.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Zhuoka Feng 1*, Kang Chen 1*, Sihan Zhao 1**, Kai Xiong **, Yaoning Wang 1** Minshen Yu 1, Junjie Nian 1, Changyi Xiao 1, Yixin Cao 1,2 † \dagger, Yugang Jiang 1. Interactive large language model agents have advanced rapidly, but most remain specialized to a single environment and fail to adapt robustly to other environments. Model merging offers a training-free alternative by integrating multiple experts into a single model.

arxiv-2601-21767.title: Evaluating ChatGPT on Medical Information Extraction Tasks: Performance, Explainability and Beyond
arxiv-2601-21767.creator: Wei Zhu
arxiv-2601-21767.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) like ChatGPT have demonstrated amazing capabilities in comprehending user intents and generate reasonable and useful responses. Beside their ability to chat, their capabilities in various natural language processing (NLP) tasks are of interest to the research community.

pmc-10648820.title: Effects of the Time of Hospice and Palliative Care Enrollment before Death on Morphine, Length of Stay, and Healthcare Expense in Patients with Cancer in Taiwan
pmc-10648820.creator: Yi-Shu Liao, Wen-Chen Tsai, Li-Ting Chiu, Pei-Tseng Kung, Paolo Cotogni
pmc-10648820.description: We aimed to investigate the effects of the time from hospice and palliative care enrollment to death on the quality of care and the effectiveness and trend of healthcare utilization in patients with terminal cancer. Data on the cancer-related mortality rates between 2005 and 2018 reported in the National Health Insurance Research Database in Taiwan were obtained.

pmc-11455667.title: Infants with biliary atresia exhibit an altered amino acid profile in their newborn screening
pmc-11455667.creator: Marie Uecker, Cornelia Prehn, Nils Janzen, Jerzy Adamski, Gertrud Vieten, Claus Petersen, Joachim F Kuebler, Omid Madadi-Sanjani, Christian Klemann
pmc-11455667.description: IntroductionBiliary atresia (BA) is a rare progressive neonatal cholangiopathy with unknown pathophysiology and time of onset. Newborn Screening (NBS) in Germany is routinely performed in the first days of life to identify rare congenital diseases utilizing dried blood spot (DBS) card analyses.

pmc-11526147.title: Lineage tracing of nuclei in skeletal myofibers uncovers distinct transcripts and interplay between myonuclear populations
pmc-11526147.creator: Chengyi Sun, Casey O Swoboda, Fabian Montecino Morales, Cristofer Calvo, Michael J Petrany, Sreeja Parameswaran, Andrew VonHandorf, Matthew T Weirauch, Christoph Lepper, Douglas P Millay
pmc-11526147.description: Multinucleated skeletal muscle cells need to acquire additional nuclei through fusion with activated skeletal muscle stem cells when responding to both developmental and adaptive growth stimuli. A fundamental question in skeletal muscle biology has been the reason underlying this need for new nuclei in cells that already harbor hundreds of nuclei.

pmc-11713840.title: Characterizing Challenges and Opportunities in Diagnostic Disclosure Communication in Dementia Care: A Qualitative Study of Clinicians
pmc-11713840.creator: Joanna Paladino, Heily Chavez Granados, Deborah Blacker, Ana‐Maria Vranceanu, Vicki Jackson, Christine S Ritchie
pmc-11713840.description: BackgroundDementia is a life‐changing condition for patients and caregivers. Response to a diagnosis often includes grief, shock, and despair. Unfortunately, evidence demonstrates inadequate use of person‐centered communication practices during diagnostic disclosure, which adds to psychological distress. Structured, person‐centered communication interventions are needed to improve the disclosure process. Our aim was to characterize communication challenges and opportunities in diagnostic disclosure.

pmc-11756559.title: The Impact of Multidisciplinary Team Intervention for Early Mobilization of Patients with Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage in Stroke Care Unit: A Retrospective Cohort Study
pmc-11756559.creator: Kenji OIKE, Osamu ISHIBASHI, Nobuyuki NOSAKA, Shin HIROTA
pmc-11756559.description: Objective: To investigate the impact of multidisciplinary team (MDT) intervention for early mobilization (EM) of patients with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH) in the intensive care unit (ICU). Methods: A retrospective uncontrolled before–after observational study was conducted to assess patient outcomes before and after introducing MDT in the stroke care unit (SCU).

pmc-12731461.title: Myocardial Scar and Cardiac Biomarker Levels as Predictors of Mortality After Acute Myocardial Infarction: A CMR-Based Long-Term Study
pmc-12731461.creator: Philipp Ruile, Johannes Brado, Klaus Kaier, Ramona Schmitt, Manuel Hein, Thomas Nührenberg, Hannah Billig, Franz-Josef Neumann, Dirk Westermann, Philipp Breitbart, Consolato M Sergi, Aw Tar-Choon
pmc-12731461.description: Background/Objectives: The extent of myocardial scar, visualized by late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) on cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR), is associated with mortality after acute myocardial infarction (MI). However, data on optimal cardiac biomarker cut-off values (e.g., high-sensitivity cardiac troponin T, hs-cTnT) for predicting LGE remain limited.

pmc-13019845.title: Global prevalence of metabolic syndrome among individuals with sarcopenia: a systematic review and meta-analysis of 72,129 patients
pmc-13019845.creator: Fei Zhang, Hang Xu, Ziwen Wang, Dishan Wu, Jinyun Wang, Zhong Wang
pmc-13019845.description: BackgroundSarcopenia is an age-related geriatric syndrome associated with an increased risk of metabolic syndrome (MS). However, the prevalence of MS among individuals with sarcopenia remains uncertain. This meta-analysis aimed to estimate the global pooled prevalence of MS in patients with sarcopenia.MethodsWe conducted the first global systematic review to quantify the prevalence of MS among people with sarcopenia.

pmc-13183184.title: Factors influencing N95 respirator use among healthcare workers in a TB specialized hospital, Bangladesh
pmc-13183184.creator: Sayeeda Tarannum, Abu-Hena Mostofa Kamal, Mohammad Tauhidul Islam, Md. Ariful Islam, Kamal Ibne Amin Chowdhury, Shirina Akhter, Afsana Sharmin, Emily S. Gurley, Sayera Banu, Md. Saiful Islam
pmc-13183184.description: BackgroundHealthcare workers (HCWs) in public tertiary care hospitals, including chest diseases hospitals, experience a substantial tuberculosis (TB) burden, with 40−48% demonstrating baseline TB infection and incidence rates of 4.2–4.8 per 100 person-years, indicating occupational exposure in high TB-burden settings. TB infection prevention and control (IPC) guidelines recommend that HCWs wear N95 respirators in pulmonary TB patient areas.

pmc-13276004.title: Quality of Primary Healthcare Services in Kazakhstan: A Systematic Review and Meta‐Analysis of Patient‐Centred Outcomes and Implications for Nursing Practice and Policy
pmc-13276004.creator: Makhabbat Shurenova, Amin Tamadon, Nadiar M Mussin, Nigora G Ashurova, Ramazon Safarzoda Sharoffidin
pmc-13276004.description: AimsTo systematically evaluate the quality, accessibility and patient‐centred performance of primary healthcare services in Kazakhstan and to generate pooled quantitative estimates of key patient‐centred and system‐level outcomes, with specific attention to their implications for primary healthcare nursing practice, nurse‐led quality improvement and nursing policy.DesignSystematic review and meta‐analysis conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines.

pmc-13456466.title: Calcium overload induces reactive oxygen species to enhance glioblastoma radiosensitivity
pmc-13456466.creator: Xin Lai, Yijun Lu, Jie Li, Lingling Liu, Shuanghu Yuan, Junchao Qian
pmc-13456466.description: Keywords: apoptosis, calcium homeostasis, calcium overload, endoplasmic reticulum stress, ionomycin, oxidative stress, protein misfolding, radiosensitization, treatment resistance, unfolded protein response Introduction The primary central nervous system malignant tumor that occurs most frequently and is the most aggressive is glioblastoma (GBM).

pmc-13544479.title: Extent of Sinus Surgery Is Associated With Disease Control in Biologic Treated Type 2 Dominant CRS
pmc-13544479.creator: Nicholas J. Campion, Peta‐Lee Sacks, Lu Hui Png, Ruoxin Hua, Rhea Darbari Kaul, Raquel Alvarado, Christine Choy, Raymond Sacks, Peter Earls, Raewyn G. Campbell, Larry Kalish, Richard J. Harvey
pmc-13544479.description: BackgroundA greater benefit of biologics is observed after surgery in Type 2 chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP). However, the extent of surgery remains undefined in many studies. This study evaluated the extent of surgery on disease control in patients receiving biologics for refractory Type 2 dominant CRSwNP.
